governanceNotes: Authored conservatively at ASSOCIATION_ONLY strength: the comorbidity evidence for Capgras syndrome and depressive symptomatology comes from a cross-sectional re-analysis within an Alzheimer's disease population (no general-population cohort) plus individual pediatric case reports, so no directional claim beyond co-occurrence is supportable at the mapping level.

Phenotype boundary respected: Capgras syndrome is a delusional misidentification phenomenon, not a mood phenotype, so the depressive-disorder target is a genuinely distinct diagnosis and this edge does not restate a diagnostic criterion (the ME-41 schizoaffective barrier does not apply).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: A cross-sectional re-analysis of the CATIE-AD cohort (421 patients with Alzheimer's disease) found Neuropsychiatric Inventory depression scores were higher among patients exhibiting Capgras syndrome than among those without it, and that Capgras syndrome was associated with the presence of depression in the severer global cognitive impairment stratum (Nagata 2024); pediatric case series document co-occurring depressive presentations in children with Capgras syndrome (Walfisch 2025).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the cross-sectional design cannot order onset, the entire quantitative evidence is internal to an Alzheimer's disease population and may not generalize to other Capgras contexts, depression in psychotic disorders has multifactorial determinants (shared neurobiology, psychosocial disability, institutional and medication effects), and no longitudinal cohort measures incident depressive disorder after Capgras onset, so no directional claim is made here.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized shared-neurocircuitry pathway has been described: Capgras syndrome is modeled as a disconnection between facial-recognition and affective-autonomic systems (familiarity without the autonomic sense of belonging), implicating ventral visual-stream and limbic circuitry; depressive comorbidity could arise either from shared limbic-dysfunctional substrate or from the profound psychosocial disruption of believing close attachment figures have been replaced by impostors, which erodes a patient's closest supportive relationships. Both pathways are mechanistically plausible in the cohort observation, but the cross-sectional data cannot separate shared-cause from consequence models, and the Alzheimer's population introduces a third confounder (dementia itself driving both phenomena), so no directional claim is made here.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. Elevated depressive symptomatology co-occurs with Capgras syndrome in a dementia-population cross-sectional analysis and in case literature, but individual determination requires psychiatric documentation of the Capgras phenomenon and of a depressive disorder meeting diagnostic criteria, with chronology and dementia-status characterization, all reviewed case by case by a qualified medical professional.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Psychiatric records documenting the Capgras delusional misidentification with onset chronology; diagnostic documentation of a depressive disorder meeting DSM criteria as a distinct episode; cognitive-status characterization (dementia versus non-dementia context) because the quantitative evidence is dementia-population specific; treatment-response history helping separate syndrome-associated mood deterioration from independent major depression; a medical professional's opinion connecting the documented findings in this individual case
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Underlying dementia or other neurodegenerative disease driving both the misidentification phenomenon and depressive symptoms
Schizophrenia-spectrum or other primary psychotic disorder with post-psychotic depression
Bereavement and psychosocial reactions to the misidentification experience itself

suggestions.rationale: Authored conservatively at association-only strength: the single quantitative record is cross-sectional within a dementia trial population, direction is undetermined, and depression in psychotic states has manifold competing determinants; the edge records co-occurrence only and leaves every causal judgment to a qualified medical professional.

sourceReferences.citation: Nagata T, Nakajima S, Kito S, Shinagawa S. The association between distinct delusional ideations and depressive symptoms in Alzheimer's disease: a re-analysis of CATIE-AD. J Alzheimers Dis. 2024;101(2):661-670. PMID 39213078. doi:10.3233/JAD-240702.
sourceReferences.note: Cross-sectional re-analysis of 421 CATIE-AD patients reporting higher Neuropsychiatric Inventory depression scores with Capgras syndrome and an association between Capgras and depression presence in the severer cognitive-impairment stratum; supports co-occurrence within a dementia population without onset ordering.

sourceReferences.citation: Walfisch R, Perlman Danieli P, Mosheva M, Eldar E, David V, Hochberg Y, Shilton T, Gothelf D. Co-existence of Capgras syndrome and OCD in children: case studies. Clin Child Psychol Psychiatry. 2025;30(3):800-808. PMID 40262183. doi:10.1177/13591045251329972.
